questions: How many call sites treat _validate_data as raising when it returns?
What does the Phase 266 accessor do when a record lacks a schema-required field?
Would making the validation fire break any existing history file?

findings.statement: _validate_data returns a list of errors and never raises; audit_history.append calls it bare and discards the result, so schema-invalid records are appended despite a docstring promising validation
audit_history.read wraps the same non-raising call in try/except ValueError, so its handler can never fire and read does not validate either; executed, read accepts a record with no ts
findings.evidence: qor/scripts/audit_history.py:85-90; probe returned the malformed record instead of raising

findings.statement: Phase 266 session_signature_timestamps is the first consumer to index record[ts], so a malformed row that was previously harmless now raises KeyError and aborts check_session_total at /qor-audit Step 0.5 and /qor-plan Step 2c
findings.evidence: executed: count_session_signature_totals OK, session_signature_timestamps KeyError, check_session_total KeyError at threshold

findings.statement: The Phase 266 plan and ledger entry #751 assert that read re-validates every line so no record can lack a well-formed ts. That guarantee does not exist and was accepted by an independent reviewer as structural
Exactly three call sites exist and only the two in audit_history are wrong; validate_gate_artifact.write_artifact checks the return and raises correctly
findings.evidence: grep over qor/: audit_history.py:53, audit_history.py:86, validate_gate_artifact.py:194-196

findings.statement: Making the validation fire is inert on live data: all 1761 rows across 189 session history files validate clean, so no existing file becomes unreadable
findings.evidence: validated every row against audit.schema.json via _validate_data

findings.statement: check_session_total builds a session path before validating session_id while its sibling check validates first; executed, check(../evil) raises ValueError and check_session_total(../evil) returns None having attempted the traversed read
